Polish pilgrims celebrate after hearing the news that the next World Youth Day will be hosted by Krakow, Poland in 2016. | Credit: Walter Sanchez Silva/EWTN News By ACI Stampa Follow + August 7, 2026 at 12:12 PM ET Polish government and Church officials have begun preparations for a possible visit by Pope Leo XIV, although no date has yet been announced. Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski met with Archbishop Tadeusz Wojda of Gdańsk, president of the Polish Bishops’ Conference, to begin coordinating preparations for what would be Leo’s first pilgrimage to Poland as pope. The papal visit would be organized jointly by the Polish government and the Catholic Church. Formal invitations have already been extended to Pope Leo XIV by both the Polish state and the Church, Vatican News reported. On behalf of the Republic of Poland, invitations have come from Presidents Andrzej Duda and Karol Nawrocki as well as Prime Minister Donald Tusk. The presidium of the Polish Bishops’ Conference has also invited the pope. Because of the international nature of the visit, Poland’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs will coordinate preparations on the government’s side. A date for the pilgrimage has not yet been determined. Once it is established, a working group composed of representatives of the relevant Church and state authorities will be created to organize the visit. Three popes have visited Poland a total of 11 times. St. John Paul II, a native of Poland, made nine papal visits to the country. Benedict XVI visited in 2006, while Pope Francis traveled to Poland in 2016 for World Youth Day in Kraków. Photograph: Bonnie Cash/UPI/Shutterstock Trump administration Trump says he is weighing suspension of federal gas tax President floats idea as voter anger over rising costs threatens Republican hopes in November midterms Joseph Gedeon in Washington Tue 6 Oct 2026 17.19 EDT Last modified on Tue 6 Oct 2026 17.21 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Donald Trump said on Tuesday his administration was considering suspending the federal gasoline tax, a sign the president is noticing voter anger over fuel costs a month before the midterm elections. “We’re thinking about that,” Trump said when asked whether the tax should be suspended. Any suspension would require an act of Congress. The president cannot unilaterally suspend the federal tax. Trump first raised the idea in May, as the Iran war pushed fuel prices sharply higher. Pump prices have stayed high since. The national average for regular was $4.3685 a gallon on Tuesday, according to AAA , more than a dollar above where it stood a year ago. The federal tax is 18.4¢ a gallon on gasoline and 24.4¢ on diesel. Dropping it would cut about 4% from the price of a gallon of regular. The tax also brings in more than $23bn a year for highways and public transit. Asked about the midterms, Trump said he expected Republicans to “do very well”. He said his rallies, were “changing things around” because voters were hearing “what the Republicans have done”. “Prices are now coming way down,” he said. “And oil, as soon as the war is over, which will be soon, will be coming way down.” He gave no date for the end of the war and did not say how a tax suspension would pass Congress.
